stories.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
stories.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
stories.acGateReason: Auto-elaborated from description (original verdict: insufficient). No acceptance criteria are provided and the description is a single vague user story with no behavioral detail, testable conditions, or error/edge case coverage.
verificationCriteria: The behavior described in the ticket is observed to be correct after the change: "[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS" (located near src/services/contentstack.ts, options).
Existing behavior related to this area is unchanged (no regression).

fixSiteAnalysis.reason: This is where the Contentstack SDK Stack is initialized. The `options` object (lines 55-67) is missing the `live_preview` config property that the Contentstack SDK requires to enable live preview of draft content. Without it, the Stack only fetches published content via the Delivery API, making CMS preview impossible. The SDK's LivePreview interface (confirmed in node_modules/contentstack/index.d.ts) requires { enable: boolean, host: string, management_token: string }.
fixSiteAnalysis.fix: Add `live_preview` config to the options object, controlled by new env vars CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ENABLE, CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST, and CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN. First, destructure these alongside the existing env vars (lines 17-24): add `CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ENABLE = '', CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST = '', CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN = ''` inside the same destructuring block. Then add a conditional `live_preview` entry to the options object after the `branch` key: `...(CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ENABLE === 'true' ? { live_preview: { enable: true, host: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST || 'api.contentstack.io', management_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN } } : {})`. The LivePreview interface is already defined in the contentstack SDK (node_modules/contentstack/index.d.ts: `interface LivePreview { host: string; management_token: string; enable: boolean }`), so no new types are needed — `contentstack.Stack(options)` already accepts it. Additionally, any page-level getServerSideProps/getStaticProps that should support preview must call `Stack.livePreviewQuery(previewData)` before fetching entries, but the prerequisite is enabling live_preview on the Stack init itself, which is this file.

specification.coordinatorNotes: Empty acceptance criteria, null spec, and cross-platform scope (GO, UP, MX) indicate a complex feature needing full elaboration then hardening. Openspec first to derive meaningful ACs from the bare title; speckit second to add testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability: Contentstack Live Preview integration. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers) — every Contentstack component delegates to it. No live-preview SDK code or config exists in the shown codebase. VCs derived from the description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty ACs with a note that this is a novel Contentstack Live Preview capability. All 14 ACs were derived from the story title, typical Contentstack Live Preview SDK behavior, and the key integration files (useContent.ts as the central hook consumed by all components, contentstack.ts as the service layer, ContentstackLink.tsx for link resolution). ACs 1-2 cover core live-preview rendering and real-time updates. AC-3 ensures published content is the default outside preview. ACs 4-6 ensure all three sites (GO, UP, MX) exhibit the same behavior. ACs 7-8 cover connection error handling and recovery. AC-9 addresses security (preventing draft content leak via URL manipulation). AC-10 addresses performance when preview is inactive. AC-11 covers ContentstackLink in preview context. AC-12 covers cleanup/teardown on navigation. AC-13 covers malformed data resilience. AC-14 covers multi-entry switching. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents, so these ACs are based on typical Contentstack Live Preview integration patterns. If useContent.ts or contentstack.ts have unusual patterns (e.g., SSR-only rendering, custom caching, different auth mechanisms), some ACs may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec performed architecture discovery (identifying useContent as the 236-caller central hook, confirming no existing Live Preview SDK code), while speckit derived 14 ACs covering core rendering, real-time updates, multi-site behavior, error handling, security, performance, link resolution, cleanup, malformed data resilience, and multi-entry switching. However, speckit explicitly states it could not read actual file contents and based all ACs on typical Contentstack Live Preview integration patterns. This is a significant risk: the 14 ACs may not align with actual codebase patterns (e.g., SSR-only rendering, custom caching, different auth mechanisms). Human review required to validate ACs against real implementation before development proceeds.
